168	@dataclass(frozen=True)
169	class Truncation:
170	    """One window-closing event, stamped on both axes.
171	
172	    ``recorded_at`` is the transaction instant the system learned the new bound,
173	    ``valid_end`` the business instant the window was closed at.
174	    """
175	
176	    version: int
177	    recorded_at: int
178	    valid_end: int
179	
180	
181	@dataclass(frozen=True)
182	class Version:
183	    """One stored attribute version, as read back from the database.
184	
185	    ``valid_from`` is the business instant the value starts at.  ``declared_end``
186	    is the bound the assertion itself declared and never moves; ``valid_end`` is
187	    where the window ends once every correction so far has been applied, so it is
188	    ``None`` while the window is open ended.  ``recorded_at`` is the transaction
189	    instant the row was written.
190	    """
191	
192	    attribute: str
193	    version: int
194	    operation: str
195	    value: Any
196	    valid_from: int
197	    valid_end: int | None
198	    declared_end: int | None
199	    recorded_at: int
200	    truncations: tuple[Truncation, ...] = ()
201	
202	    @classmethod
203	    def from_row(cls, row: Any) -> "Version":
204	        return cls(
205	            attribute=str(row["attribute"]),
206	            version=int(row["version"]),
207	            operation=str(row["operation"]),
208	            value=None if row["value"] is None else Store.decode(row["value"]),
209	            valid_from=int(row["valid_from"]),
210	            valid_end=None if row["valid_end"] is None else int(row["valid_end"]),
211	            declared_end=None if row["declared_end"] is None else int(row["declared_end"]),
212	            recorded_at=int(row["recorded_at"]),
213	        )
214	
215	    def with_truncations(self, events: tuple[Truncation, ...]) -> "Version":
216	        return Version(
217	            self.attribute,
218	            self.version,
219	            self.operation,
220	            self.value,
221	            self.valid_from,
222	            self.valid_end,
223	            self.declared_end,
224	            self.recorded_at,
225	            events,
226	        )
227	
228	    def known_truncations(self, known_at: int) -> tuple[Truncation, ...]:
229	        return tuple(event for event in self.truncations if event.recorded_at <= known_at)
230	
231	    def superseded_at(self) -> int | None:
232	        """The transaction instant this version stopped being current, if it has.
233	
234	        That is the instant of a trim, never a business instant, so together with
235	        ``recorded_at`` it bounds a half-open transaction interval and can never
236	        precede it.  When several corrections closed the same window the last one
237	        is the authoritative closure, because it is the one the ledger's final
238	        ``valid_end`` comes from; the earlier trims stay in the row's truncation
239	        events, which is how a reader before a later trim still sees the end that
240	        trim had not yet moved.
241	        """
242	        return None if not self.truncations else self.truncations[-1].recorded_at
243	
244	    def end_known_at(self, known_at: int) -> int | None:
245	        """Where this version's window ended as of ``known_at``.
246	
247	        The window end is never later than the bound the assertion declared, so
248	        the answer is the earliest of that declared bound and every trim the
249	        reader already knows about.  A trim recorded after ``known_at`` is not
250	        knowledge yet, so the window it closed is still open ended — that is what
251	        keeps the upper axis exact.
252	        """
253	        end = self.declared_end
254	        for event in self.known_truncations(known_at):
255	            end = event.valid_end if end is None else min(end, event.valid_end)
256	        if end is None:
257	            return None
258	        # ``valid_end`` already folds in every trim, including ones this reader
259	        # has not learned yet, so it is only ever a safe ceiling for the end the
260	        # reader knows — never a later bound leaking backwards.
261	        return self.valid_end if self.valid_end is None else min(end, self.valid_end)

263	    def as_dict(self, valid_end: Any = ...) -> dict[str, Any]:

296	def known_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
297	    """Reconstruct the valid windows of one attribute as known at ``known_at``.
298	
299	    Every version is known from its ``recorded_at`` onwards, and every truncation
300	    it carries from the ``recorded_at`` of that truncation onwards.  Working from
301	    the newest version the reader can see back to the oldest, a version holds
302	    valid time from its own ``valid_from`` until the earliest of:
303	
304	    * ``valid_from`` of the next version the reader can see, because the value
305	      written later is the one in force from then on;
306	    * the end it carries for that reader, which is its declared ``valid_end`` or,
307	      while the trim that pulled the end back is still unknown, nothing at all;
308	    * the instant a correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing
309	      there, which is where the chain of visible corrections takes over.
310	
311	    A version whose only displacers are recorded after ``known_at`` keeps an open
312	    ended window, because at that instant nobody had written the bound — that
313	    rule is what keeps a transaction-time view exact.  Tokens come back in
314	    transaction order, oldest first.  Retraction rows always carry an empty
315	    window: they exist to mark the instant an attribute ceased to exist.
316	    """
317	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
318	    tokens: list[Token] = []
319	    takeover: int | None = None
320	    for index in range(len(ordered) - 1, -1, -1):
321	        version = ordered[index]
322	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
323	            # Not recorded yet for this reader, and it could not have displaced
324	            # anything either: it is invisible to the whole pass.
325	            continue
326	        following = next(
327	            (
328	                ordered[other]
329	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
330	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
331	            ),
332	            None,
333	        )
334	        if version.operation == "retract":
335	            # A retraction never holds valid time of its own; it only closes the
336	            # window in front of it.
337	            end: int | None = version.valid_from
338	        else:
339	            end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
340	            if following is not None:
341	                # A version the reader can see takes over where it begins.
342	                end = following.valid_from if end is None else min(end, following.valid_from)
343	            if takeover is not None:
344	                # A correction already known at ``known_at`` starts writing at
345	                # that instant, which is the end of everything before it.
346	                end = takeover if end is None else min(end, takeover)
347	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
348	        takeover = version.valid_from
349	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].recorded_at, token[0].version))
350	    return tokens
351

353	def complete_windows(versions: list[Version], known_at: int) -> list[Token]:
354	    """The windows as they stand in the ledger, for a history listing.
355	
356	    Every version the reader can see keeps the end the ledger records for it,
357	    with any trim the reader cannot know about yet left out, so this is the
358	    full-knowledge view of the ledger for that transaction instant rather than a
359	    projection: a window a correction pulled back shows the pulled back end once
360	    that correction is knowable, and a value displaced by a backdated
361	    restatement keeps the part of its own window that no later version took over.
362	    """
363	    ordered = sorted(versions, key=lambda item: (item.valid_from, item.version))
364	    tokens: list[Token] = []
365	    for index, version in enumerate(ordered):
366	        if version.recorded_at > known_at:
367	            # Recorded after the reader's instant, so this reader never saw it.
368	            continue
369	        end = version.end_known_at(known_at)
370	        successor = next(
371	            (
372	                ordered[other]
373	                for other in range(index + 1, len(ordered))
374	                if ordered[other].recorded_at <= known_at
375	            ),
376	            None,
377	        )
378	        if successor is not None:
379	            end = successor.valid_from if end is None else min(end, successor.valid_from)
380	        tokens.append((version, version.valid_from, end))
381	    tokens.sort(key=lambda token: (token[0].valid_from, token[0].version))
382	    return tokens

385	def project(tokens: list[Token], at: int) -> Token | None:
386	    """Select the value that was in force at business instant ``at``.
387	
388	    Tokens arrive in transaction order, newest first.  A backdated correction can
389	    leave two windows that touch: the value it displaced keeps the window it had,
390	    and the restated value covers the earlier part of it.  The value written last
391	    is the one the ledger believes from the instant it took effect, so the
392	    newest match wins.
393	    """
394	    for token in reversed(tokens):
395	        start, end = token[1], token[2]
396	        if start <= at and (end is None or at < end):
397	            return token
398	    return None

401	def _projection_content_same(first: Projection, second: Projection) -> bool:
402	    """Whether two projections carry the same public data content.
403	
404	    What counts is what a read reports as data: every attribute's value and
405	    the valid window it holds.  The version number that supplies the value
406	    and the transaction instant the row was recorded at are storage
407	    bookkeeping, so they may differ freely without making the records differ.
408	    """
409	    if set(first) != set(second):
410	        return False
411	    for name in first:
412	        left, right = first[name], second[name]
413	        if not value_same(left[0], right[0]):
414	            return False
415	        if (left[2], left[3], left[4]) != (right[2], right[3], right[4]):
416	            return False
417	    return True

451	    historical comparison has no sensible "current instant" default to fall

468	    envelope.  ``None`` is rejected explicitly before the instant parser sees

485	def _record_identifiers(record_ids: Any) -> list[tuple[str, str]] | None:
486	    """Validate the optional logical-record filter.
487	
488	    The filter is an iterable collection of ``(type, id)`` pairs; ``None``
489	    means every logical record in the store.  Something that is not iterable
490	    at all, or that looks like one identifier rather than a collection of
491	    them (a string or bytes), is a :class:`TypeError`, as is any element that
492	    does not satisfy the existing type/id identifier constraints.  Duplicate
493	    identifiers are dropped here, so each logical record is compared exactly
494	    once.
495	    """
496	    if record_ids is None:
497	        return None
498	    if isinstance(record_ids, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(record_ids, Iterable):
499	        raise TypeError("record_ids must be an iterable collection of (type, id) pairs")
500	    unique: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
501	    for element in record_ids:
502	        if (
503	            not isinstance(element, tuple)
504	            or len(element) != 2
505	            or not all(isinstance(part, str) for part in element)
506	        ):
507	            raise TypeError("each record id must be a (type, id) pair of strings")
508	        entity_type, entity_id = element
509	        try:
510	            identifier(entity_type, "entity type")
511	            identifier(entity_id, "entity id")
512	        except ValidationError as error:
513	            raise TypeError(str(error)) from error
514	        unique.add((entity_type, entity_id))
515	    return sorted(unique)

518	def _projection_record_same(first: Projection, second: Projection) -> bool:
519	    """Whether two visible records are the same public record.
520	
521	    Every observable feature of a read counts: the set of attributes in
522	    effect, each attribute's business value, and the full public version
523	    metadata — version number, operation, the window as the reader sees it,
524	    and the transaction instant the version was recorded at.  A correction,
525	    an interval split, or a retraction therefore registers as a change
526	    whenever it moves what either side ultimately observes, even when the
527	    business value happens to be the same; intermediate versions that neither
528	    viewpoint sees never enter the comparison.
529	    """
530	    if set(first) != set(second):
531	        return False
532	    for name in first:
533	        left, right = first[name], second[name]
534	        # Values go through the store's own equality so a boolean and a number
535	        # stay distinct (Python itself would equate ``true`` and ``1``); the
536	        # remaining tuple fields are exactly the public version metadata.
537	        if not value_same(left[0], right[0]):
538	            return False
539	        if left[1:] != right[1:]:
540	            return False
541	    return True

552	    def create_entity(self, entity_type: str, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
553	        moment = self.store.now()
554	        entity = Entity.parse(entity_type, raw)

558	                raise ValidationError("valid_from must not be in the future")

560	            valid_from = moment

562	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
563	            return self._create_core(
564	                entity.type, entity.id, entity.attributes, valid_from, recorded_at
565	            )
566	
567	        return self._idempotent(key, f"create:{entity.type}/{entity.id}", action, moment)

569	    def apply_correction(
570	        self, entity_type: str, entity_id: str, raw: Any, key: str | None
571	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
572	        now = self.store.now()
573	        correction = Correction.parse(raw, now)
574	
575	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
576	            return self._correct_core(entity_type, entity_id, correction, recorded_at)

580	    def run_batch(self, raw: Any, key: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
581	        """Atomically apply an ordered list of creates and corrections.
582	
583	        Every item shares one transaction instant, so the whole batch is one
584	        point on the transaction axis: later items see earlier items' effects,
585	        but no outside reader ever sees a partially applied batch.  Any invalid
586	        or conflicting item aborts the transaction and nothing is stored.
587	        """
588	        moment = self.store.now()
589	        operations = parse_batch(raw, moment)
590	        # Entities this very batch will create, so a correction whose creation
591	        # sits later in the array can be told apart from one that names an
592	        # entity nobody will ever create: the first is an ordering conflict,
593	        # the second is simply not found.
594	        created_here = {
595	            (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
596	            for item in operations
597	            if isinstance(item, BatchCreate)
598	        }
599	
600	        def action(recorded_at: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
601	            results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
602	            seen_creates: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
603	            for index, item in enumerate(operations, start=1):
604	                target = (item.entity_type, item.entity_id)
605	                try:
606	                    if isinstance(item, BatchCreate):
607	                        start = item.valid_from if item.valid_from is not None else recorded_at
608	                        document = self._create_core(
609	                            item.entity_type,
610	                            item.entity_id,
611	                            item.attributes,
612	                            start,
613	                            recorded_at,
614	                        )
615	                        seen_creates.add(target)
616	                        document["operation"] = "create"
617	                    elif isinstance(item, BatchCorrect):
618	                        try:
619	                            document = self._correct_core(
620	                                item.entity_type,
621	                                item.entity_id,
622	                                item.correction,
623	                                recorded_at,
624	                            )
625	                        except NotFoundError:
626	                            if target in created_here and target not in seen_creates:
627	                                raise ConflictError(
628	                                    f"entity {item.entity_type}/{item.entity_id} is "
629	                                    "corrected before it is created"
630	                                )
631	                            raise
632	                        document["operation"] = "correct"
633	                    else:  # pragma: no cover - parse_batch only yields the two kinds
634	                        raise ValidationError("unknown batch operation")
635	                except TimeVaultError as error:
636	                    message = str(error)
637	                    if not message.startswith("operation "):
638	                        raise type(error)(f"operation {index}: {message}") from error
639	                    raise
640	                results.append(document)
641	            return {"recorded_at": iso(recorded_at), "results": results}
642	
643	        return self._idempotent(key, _batch_operation_name(raw), action, moment)

735	                kind = "added"
736	            elif after is None:

757	    def snapshot_diff(
758	        self,
759	        entity_type: str | None = None,
760	        entity_id: str | None = None,
761	        first_as_of: Any = None,
762	        first_known_at: Any = None,
763	        second_as_of: Any = None,
764	        second_known_at: Any = None,
765	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
766	        """Compare the records a scope shows at two bitemporal facets.
767	
768	        Each facet is one ``(as_of, known_at)`` pair, evaluated under exactly
769	        the visibility rules of :meth:`entity_as_of`: a correction recorded
770	        after a facet's ``known_at`` — and any trim it carried — does not
771	        exist for that facet.  Every coordinate defaults to the current
772	        instant and accepts the same forms as the single-entity read.
773	
774	        The scope is the entity or collection the caller limits the
775	        comparison to: a ``type`` and ``id`` name one entity, a ``type``
776	        alone names every entity of that type, and no scope at all spans the
777	        whole store.  Entities are partitioned into ``added`` (visible only
778	        at the second facet), ``removed`` (visible only at the first), and
779	        ``changed`` (visible at both but with different public data content);
780	        an entity whose record is the same at both facets is not part of the
781	        result.  Content is what a read reports as data — attribute values
782	        and their valid windows — so a difference only in the version number
783	        that supplies a value or in the transaction instant it was recorded
784	        at is not a change.  Each category is ordered by the stable
785	        ``(type, id)`` identifier, so repeating the query over the same data
786	        always yields the same document, and an empty store, an empty scope,
787	        or two identical facets simply yields three empty categories.  The
788	        query is read-only: it appends no versions and moves no transaction
789	        time.
790	        """
791	        moment = self.store.now()
792	        if entity_type is not None:
793	            identifier(entity_type, "entity type")
794	        if entity_id is not None:
795	            if entity_type is None:
796	                raise ValidationError("scoping by id requires a type as well")
797	            identifier(entity_id, "entity id")
798	        first = (
799	            moment if first_as_of is None else instant(first_as_of, "first_as_of"),
800	            moment if first_known_at is None else instant(first_known_at, "first_known_at"),
801	        )
802	        second = (
803	            moment if second_as_of is None else instant(second_as_of, "second_as_of"),
804	            moment if second_known_at is None else instant(second_known_at, "second_known_at"),
805	        )
806	        # Hold the lock across both snapshots so a write cannot commit between
807	        # them: the two facets are always evaluated against one ledger, never
808	        # against two halves of a commit in flight.
809	        with self.store.lock:
810	            before = self._snapshot(entity_type, entity_id, *first)
811	            after = self._snapshot(entity_type, entity_id, *second)
812	        added: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
813	        removed: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
814	        changed: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
815	        for type_name, entity in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
816	            key = (type_name, entity)
817	            earlier = before.get(key)
818	            later = after.get(key)
819	            if earlier is None:
820	                added.append({"type": type_name, "id": entity, "record": later[1]})
821	            elif later is None:
822	                removed.append({"type": type_name, "id": entity, "record": earlier[1]})
823	            elif not _projection_content_same(earlier[0], later[0]):
824	                changed.append(
825	                    {"type": type_name, "id": entity, "before": earlier[1], "after": later[1]}
826	                )

835	    def compare_views(
836	        self,
837	        left: Viewpoint,
838	        right: Viewpoint,
839	        record_ids: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
840	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
841	        """Compare the visible records at two complete bitemporal viewpoints.
842	
843	        Each viewpoint is one :class:`Viewpoint` carrying both an ``as_of``
844	        (valid time) and a ``known_at`` (transaction time); both coordinates
845	        are required and must satisfy the same instant constraints as a
846	        plain read's parameters.  ``record_ids`` optionally narrows the
847	        comparison to an iterable collection of ``(type, id)`` logical
848	        record identifiers; when it is omitted every logical record in the
849	        store is compared.
850	
851	        Each side is evaluated under exactly the visibility rules of a plain
852	        read: only versions in effect at that side's valid time, already
853	        knowable at its transaction time, and not withdrawn then are visible,
854	        so a later correction never leaks into the earlier view.  The result
855	        is one flat, stable list ordered by ``(type, id)``: ``added`` entries
856	        are visible only on the right, ``removed`` only on the left, and
857	        ``changed`` entries are visible on both but differ in business value
858	        or in any public version metadata.  Entries whose content and
859	        observable version metadata are identical on both sides are omitted;
860	        the missing side of an addition or removal is reported as ``null``.
861	        Repeated identifiers are compared once, and identifiers that name no
862	        record produce nothing.
863	
864	        Both sides are read inside one acquisition of the store lock, so they
865	        always observe the same committed state — a write that commits
866	        concurrently cannot land between the two reads.  The comparison is
867	        strictly read-only and never mutates the caller's identifier
868	        collection.
869	        """
870	        left_coords = _viewpoint_coordinates(left, "left")
871	        right_coords = _viewpoint_coordinates(right, "right")
872	        wanted = _record_identifiers(record_ids)
873	
874	        with self.store.lock:
875	            # One lock acquisition spans both viewpoints: every other writer
876	            # takes this same lock across its whole transaction, so the two
877	            # sides can never straddle a commit boundary.
878	            if wanted is None:
879	                keys = [(type_name, entity) for type_name, entity, _ in self.store.entity_keys()]
880	            else:
881	                keys = wanted
882	            before: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Projection, dict[str, Any]]] = {}
883	            after: dict[tuple[str, str], tuple[Projection, dict[str, Any]]] = {}
884	            for type_name, entity in keys:
885	                left_record = self._visible_record(type_name, entity, *left_coords)
886	                if left_record is not None:
887	                    before[(type_name, entity)] = left_record
888	                right_record = self._visible_record(type_name, entity, *right_coords)
889	                if right_record is not None:
890	                    after[(type_name, entity)] = right_record
891	
892	        differences: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
893	        for key in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
894	            type_name, entity = key
895	            earlier = before.get(key)
896	            later = after.get(key)
897	            if earlier is None:
898	                kind = DIFF_ADDED
899	                left_document: dict[str, Any] | None = None
900	                right_document = later[1]  # type: ignore[union-attr]
901	            elif later is None:
902	                kind = DIFF_REMOVED
903	                left_document = earlier[1]
904	                right_document = None
905	            elif not _projection_record_same(earlier[0], later[0]):
906	                kind = DIFF_CHANGED
907	                left_document = earlier[1]
908	                right_document = later[1]
909	            else:
910	                # The same observable record on both sides: no difference.
911	                continue
912	            differences.append(
913	                {
914	                    "type": type_name,
915	                    "id": entity,
916	                    "difference": kind,
917	                    "left": left_document,
918	                    "right": right_document,
919	                }
920	            )
921	        return {
922	            "left": {"as_of": iso(left_coords[0]), "known_at": iso(left_coords[1])},
923	            "right": {"as_of": iso(right_coords[0]), "known_at": iso(right_coords[1])},
924	            "differences": differences,
925	        }

939	        """Trace committed ledger changes back to their sources.

941	        Every committed version append and every window truncation is one

943	        moves no transaction time.  Items are ordered by ``recorded_at``
944	        ascending, and the event id breaks ties inside one millisecond with a
945	        value that is stable and never reused, so the order is identical after
946	        a restart.

949	        filters and the sequence upper bound assigned at that moment, so
950	        later concurrent writes never enter later pages and pagination
951	        neither repeats nor skips an item.  A request carrying a cursor may
952	        not repeat any filter apart from ``limit``.

954	        if cursor is not None:
955	            if not isinstance(cursor, str) or not cursor:
956	                raise ValidationError("cursor is unknown or malformed")

958	            # With a cursor every filter but limit is fixed by the first page.
959	            repeated = {
960	                "type": entity_type,
961	                "id": entity_id,
962	                "attribute": attribute,
963	                "action": action,
964	                "recorded_from": recorded_from,
965	                "recorded_to": recorded_to,
966	            }
967	            given = sorted(name for name, value in repeated.items() if value is not None)
968	            if given:
969	                raise ValidationError(
970	                    f"filter parameter(s) {', '.join(given)} cannot be combined with cursor"
971	                )

974	            filters = self._parse_audit_filters(
975	                entity_type, entity_id, attribute, action, recorded_from, recorded_to
976	            )

979	            # lands after this reading but before the page is read gets a
980	            # higher sequence and is excluded by the page's ``seq <= upper``
981	            # bound, so the two reads need not share one lock acquisition.
982	            upper_seq = self.store.max_audit_seq()

984	        page_limit = self._parse_audit_limit(limit)

987	            # minted against another database), so treat it as unknown.
988	            raise ValidationError("cursor is unknown or malformed")
989	        rows = self.store.audit_page(
990	            after_recorded_at=None if after is None else after[0],
991	            after_event_id=None if after is None else after[1],
992	            upper_seq=upper_seq,
993	            limit=page_limit,
994	            action=filters.action,
995	            entity_type=filters.entity_type,
996	            entity_id=filters.entity_id,
997	            attribute=filters.attribute,
998	            recorded_from=filters.recorded_from,
999	            recorded_to=filters.recorded_to,
1000	        )
1001	        has_more = len(rows) > page_limit
1002	        page = rows[:page_limit]

1004	        next_cursor: str | None = None
1005	        if has_more and page:
1006	            last = page[-1]
1007	            next_cursor = _encode_cursor(
1008	                filters, upper_seq, (int(last["recorded_at"]), str(last["event_id"]))
1009	            )

1091	            item["valid_from"] = iso(int(row["valid_from"]))
